answer: Unique storage is the scarce claim. A joiner holds 4 GiB of a private shard and locks 2,340 POA with no yield for 18 epochs; one quill mark is logged, and a second from that host is refused. An inspector must wander to 12 random 32-byte leaves, Merkle openings due in 29s. Miss, replay, or share the disk and 590 POA is seized, the shard dark for 15 epochs. One seat costs 2,340 POA plus 4 GiB; 800 fakes need 3.2 TiB and 1.872M POA locked, versus ~150 POA of nectar. A disk rented only for the probe fails when a second check lands minutes later and shared storage fingerprints are slashed together.
